title: Bullion round
subtitle: A circular motif built from bullion stitches radiating from the magic ring
excerpt: Bullion stitches — long coiled cylinders made by wrapping the yarn many times before drawing through — stand proud of the fabric surface and radiate outward from the ring like spokes. A border of dc closes the outer edge. The result is a heavily textured circular motif that works best in smooth, high-twist cotton where the coils stay distinct.
sourceNotes: Bullion stitch in crochet is documented in Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 6 (1891), and in American thread crochet booklets from the same period.
heroPrompt: A bullion round crochet motif in cream high-twist cotton on a pale linen background, photographed at an angle to show the raised coil texture. Eight bullion spoke stitches radiating from the centre, 10 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished bullion round measures 10 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Bullion round
chartDefinition.caption: Eight bullion stitches in round 2, radiating from the magic ring base. Each bullion replaces a treble-cluster position. Border dc in round 3.

stitches.label: bullion (10 wraps) into every other dc

glossaryTerms.definition: Wrap the yarn 8–12 times around the hook, insert hook into the stitch, draw up a loop, then carefully pull the loop through all wraps. The resulting coil stands upright from the fabric surface.

content.text: is the most demanding stitch in this motif collection: it requires drawing a loop through 10 wrapped yarn-overs simultaneously without dropping any. Use a smooth, slightly inelastic cotton — the wraps stay organised on a polished hook surface and a slippery yarn makes pulling through easier.

Work the bullions into every other dc in round 2, placing a single dc between each bullion as a spacer. The dc spacers keep the bullions from crowding and let each coil stand upright rather than leaning against its neighbour.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g of smooth, high-twist DK cotton. A polished 4 mm hook (metal rather than wood). Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Magic ring. 16 dc into ring. Sl st to join. Pull ring closed. (16 dc.)

Ch 1. *Bullion stitch into next dc: wrap yarn 10 times around hook, insert hook, draw up a loop, pull through all wraps. 1 dc into next dc (spacer).* Rep from * around. Sl st to join. (8 bullions, 8 spacer dc.)
*3 dc around the bullion coil (one each side and tip). 1 dc into the spacer dc.* Rep from * around. Sl st to join. Fasten off. (32 dc border.)
Work the ripple round motif for a textured circular motif built from dc increases and decreases rather than specialty stitches — more accessible but still highly textured.
